english: Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}-110x+1000}$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x-10}\,\sqrt{x-100}$, each defined on the set of all real numbers $x$ for which its expression is a real number. Let $D$ be the largest subset of $\mathbb{R}$ on which $f$ and $g$ are identical functions, and let $h:D\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $h(x)=x+\dfrac{2500}{x}$. Then the least value of $h$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}-110x+1000}$ तथा $g(x)=\sqrt{x-10}\,\sqrt{x-100}$ हैं, जिनमें से प्रत्येक उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ के समुच्चय पर परिभाषित है जिनके लिए उसका व्यंजक एक वास्तविक संख्या है। माना कि $D$, $\mathbb{R}$ का वह सबसे बड़ा उपसमुच्चय है जिस पर $f$ तथा $g$ सर्वसम फलन हैं, तथा $h:D\to\mathbb{R}$, $h(x)=x+\dfrac{2500}{x}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $h$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: $x^{2}-110x+1000=(x-10)(x-100)$: domain of $f$ is $(-\infty,10]\cup[100,\infty)$; domain of $g$ needs $x\ge10$ and $x\ge100$, i.e. $[100,\infty)$
On $[100,\infty)$ both factors are $\ge0$, so $\sqrt{x-10}\sqrt{x-100}=\sqrt{(x-10)(x-100)}$; for $x\le10$ only $f$ is defined
$h'(x)=1-\dfrac{2500}{x^{2}}>0$ for $x>50$, so $h$ is increasing on $D$ and its range is $[h(100),\infty)$
solution_full: Since $x^{2}-110x+1000=(x-10)(x-100)$, $f$ is defined when $(x-10)(x-100)\ge0$, i.e. on $(-\infty,10]\cup[100,\infty)$.
$g$ is defined when both $x-10\ge0$ and $x-100\ge0$, i.e. on $[100,\infty)$.

Two functions are identical on a set when both are defined there and agree at every point. For $x\ge100$, both $x-10$ and $x-100$ are non-negative, so $\sqrt{x-10}\,\sqrt{x-100}=\sqrt{(x-10)(x-100)}$ and $f(x)=g(x)$. For $x\le10$, $g$ is not defined. Hence $D=[100,\infty)$.
On $(0,\infty)$, AM-GM gives $x+\dfrac{2500}{x}\ge2\sqrt{2500}=100$, with equality only at $x=50$. But $50\notin D$, so this bound is not attained on $D$.
$h'(x)=1-\dfrac{2500}{x^{2}}=\dfrac{(x-50)(x+50)}{x^{2}}>0$ for $x>50$, so $h$ is strictly increasing on $D=[100,\infty)$, and $h(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$.
Hence the range of $h$ is $[h(100),\infty)=[125,\infty)$, since $h(100)=100+\dfrac{2500}{100}=125$. The least value of $h$ is $125$.
originality_note: New: the domain of the range problem is the set on which two radical expressions are identical, and that set excludes the AM-GM equality point, so the minimum moves to the boundary (way 5). Closest known: 'find x for which sqrt(ab) = sqrt(a) sqrt(b)' and AM-GM minimum of x + k/x. Different because: the identical-function domain cuts off the AM-GM point; the AM-GM value 100 is the trap.

concept_use.Definition of a function; vertical line: D is the largest set on which f and g are identical: both defined and equal, which is [100, infinity).
concept_use.Domain of algebraic, logarithmic, expone: The radical domains (x - 10)(x - 100) >= 0 for f and x >= 10, x >= 100 for g decide D.
concept_use.Range by inverse method, boundedness, AM: Range of h = x + 2500/x on D: AM-GM gives 100 only at x = 50 outside D, so h is increasing on D and its range is [125, infinity).
